text: Lalit Mohan Sharma (12 February 1928 – 3 November 2008) was the 24th Chief Justice of India, serving for 85 days from 18 November 1992 until 11 February 1993. He was the son of L.N. Sinha, who served as Attorney General of India during Indira Gandhi's tenure as Prime Minister and as Solicitor General of India from 17 July 1972 to 5 April 1977. Born in Musi (Belaganj, Gaya, Bihar) into a Bhumihar family, Sharma obtained a B.A. Hons. from Patna University in 1946 and a B.L. from the same university in 1948. He enrolled as an articled clerk in the Patna High Court in 1949 and began practicing as an Advocate in the Patna High Court on 6 February 1950. He was enrolled as a Supreme Court Advocate on 6 March 1957 and later designated as a Senior Advocate. He took charge as a Judge of the Patna High Court on 12 April 1973. Sharma joined the Supreme Court of India on 5 October 1987 and authored 157 judgments while sitting on 406 benches during his tenure. He was appointed Chief Justice of India on 18 November 1992 and retired from the judicial service on 11 February 1993. Sharma passed away on 3 November 2008 in Patna at his residence after a long illness at the age of 80. He is survived by his wife, son, and daughter. His son, Justice Partha Sarthy, currently serves as a Judge in the Patna High Court.
